searchText: I;d personally try to 1. avoid binary curve 2. use a curve with prime order what's the max value in bits for 'p' you are looking for <@755590043632140352> ? There's no 1 and 2, I need both properties 😄 I need any such combination that is better than Ristretto. Qualitatively we have: - the faster the curve the better CPU performance is - the smaller the p the better bandwidth is. I prefer the second as long as it doesn't really take a big toll on the first one sorry for the misunderstanding 1. and 2. were "my 2 suggestions" about p i would not go under 64 bits (max of the stretch i would concede) we could create such a curve with Complex Multiplication in order to enable the GLV endomorphism fairly easily but it is well known that for MSM GLV advantage decreases with the amount of entries... (this would also apply to GLS curve for the record...) I guess <@755590043632140352> was looking for something already **implemented**. I suspect that a brand new curve is less interesting here. i do not think there is any curve in production over F_p^r with small p and big r (at the net of r =2) I don't mind implementing myself the assembly if it satisfies the two properties above. <@750602516613431366> why not under 64 bit? I myself have no conditions on it. For my application 8 bits are more than enough because well security https://hal.science/hal-01981526/document 🙂 this is how a curve built over 26 bit field extension got broken many years ago so i think something along 64 bits is the minimum I'd be able to risk (personally) Just to be very clear, is the claim that commitments over F_q with q = p^r and p small, but r >> 0 can be forged probably? or is it the claim only for r=1? I need the commitments to be secure, but the coefficients can be on a very small subfield of F_q Oh that article seems to claim this in great generality.... hmm if the statement above is true (about 64 bits) then perhaps Ristretto is already good enough, I'd get maximum a reduction by 4) that article brakes ECDLP for curve with characteristic q = p^r with p being 27 bits so more general than pedersen commitment

There's no 1 and 2, I need both properties 😄 I need any such combination that is better than Ristretto. Qualitatively we have: 
- the faster the curve the better CPU performance is
- the smaller the p the better bandwidth is. 

I prefer the second as long as it doesn't really take a big toll on the first one
